summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis, anxiety, and probable sphincter of Oddi dysfunction was admitted with epigastric pain and nausea following an MRCP with secretin, which triggered an acute flare of pancreatitis. She was managed conservatively with NPO status, IV fluids, Dilaudid for pain, and Reglan for nausea, avoiding Zofran due to allergy. Her lipase levels improved, and she gradually advanced to a soft diet without complications. MRCP findings confirmed chronic pancreatitis and possible sphincter of Oddi dysfunction, prompting GI consultation and plans for outpatient EUS. Her psychiatric medications were continued, with adjustments to fluoxetine. She remained pain-free, ambulatory, and mentally clear, and was discharged home with a low-fat diet plan, pain and nausea medications, and follow-up arranged with gastroenterology.
